Read only current facts and return the schema value, not a service_events wrapper. Represent each source service clause as one service_relations item. Keep coordinated workers together when one clause assigns them the same employer, service kind, location, and service period. For “X paid A, B, and C for labor,” workers=[A,B,C] and employer=X. For “A and B were paid for services performed for X,” workers=[A,B] and employer=X. For direct performance language, preserve the explicitly named performer and beneficiary/employer. Do not infer an employer merely from proximity.

The grammar field records which licensed role construction established the relation; it is factual provenance, not query identity. Preserve the explicit service_term and only normalize kind when its meaning is clear. Locations, venue categories, and countries must be attached to this service clause and must not be copied from education, residence, payment, or another service.

The period object is independent of identity. Use interval only for two service-specific full dates, date only for one service-specific full date, and year_only only when a year grammatically modifies the service itself. A payment year before “for services,” an annual amount year, a native workday, or enrollment/attendance dates do not modify the service and must leave period.status=not_stated. Never synthesize January 1 or December 31 from a year.

Use exact nonempty facts witnesses. Scan every sentence independently so that a following reversal of payer and worker or a different kind/period remains a distinct relation. If any service-language construction has unresolved coordination, attachment, voice, employer, or period, return unread and null rather than omitting it or claiming an empty complete scan. Complete empty is permitted only when the finite facts contain no service-language cue. No question, query, statute, source ID, answer, annotation, or previous example is available. Do not output query flags or legal conclusions.
Shared native event meanings: Shared factual encoding from the author statute program:
service_(event), agent_(service,worker), patient_(service,employer).
payment_(event), agent_(payment,payer), patient_(payment,payee),
purpose_(payment,service_event), amount_(payment,amount).
purpose_(service,"domestic service"|"agricultural labor") is a stated service kind.
marriage_(event) has an agent_ fact for EACH spouse.
death_(event) has agent_(event,deceased), start_(event,actual_death_date).
enrollment_(event) has agent_(event,student), patient_(event,institution).
attending_classes_(event) has agent_(event,student), location_(event,institution).
educational_institution_(event) has agent_(event,institution).
income_(event) has agent_(event,recipient), amount_(event,amount).
start_/end_ describe the dates/period of that SAME event, not arbitrary dates
belonging to a different event. A stated annual income can be represented over
its stated calendar year with canonical year bounds; this does not invent the
date of an instantaneous payment. Never allocate a cross-year payment or give
it a payment date copied from a service period without support.

Explicit source-stated intermediate legal givens, with ordered arguments:
s151_b_applies(taxpayer:string,spouse:string,year:integer)
s151_c_applies(taxpayer:string,dependent:string,year:integer)
s63_f_1_A(taxpayer:string,year:integer)
s63_f_1_B(taxpayer:string,spouse:string,year:integer)
s151_b(taxpayer:string,exemption_amount:number,year:integer)
s152_c_1(dependent:string,taxpayer:string,year:integer)
Keep source polarity and taxpayer/beneficiary direction. A151(d) statement is not automatically a151(b)/(c) fact. Never assert the target predicate or infer unstated ages, deaths or relationships. This is shared infrastructure, not learned legal knowledge.
